- Auto-update logic needs revision:
  - Currently interrupting active chats
  - Need to expand “do not update” conditions beyond meetings

### Customer Pain Points

- Note ownership/transfer challenges:
  - Increased requests for email transfer/changes
  - Legal constraints prevent transfers without proof of ownership
  - Individual plan notes belong to users
  - Business/Enterprise plan notes belong to company
- Windows performance issues persist:
  - Reports of crashes
  - General slowdown complaints
- Japanese character input bug identified:
  - Characters appearing at start of input
  - Priority fix needed

### Language Support Rollout

- Current usage: \~2,000 users
- Initial feedback:
  - Generally positive response
  - Portuguese localization issues (PT-PT vs PT-BR)
  - Transcription accuracy concerns in some languages
  - Summaries performing well despite transcription issues

### Feature Requests & Feedback

- Folders feature feedback:
  - Multiple note versions issue when multiple attendees take notes
  - User concerns about note quality comparisons
- Continued requests for:
  - Multi-language support improvements
  - Windows folders enhancements
  - Detailed transcription notes
  - Chat history
  - Outlook/Office integration
  - Export/import capabilities
- Diarization priority:
  - Users prioritizing diarization over real-time transcription
  - Some iPhone users using mobile app audio capture for better diarization

### Metrics & Performance

- App Store Performance:
  - U.S. ratings: 290 ratings with 5-star average
  - Positive review stream across all regions
  - Dedicated channel established for review monitoring

2025-04-10T14:13:01.877Z
User Interviews
### Background Information

- Raphael is a software engineer since 2020
- Currently works at a company (9-10 employees) building B2B app for heat pump installers
- App helps manage installation workflows, CRM, site surveys, and delivery processes
- Joined current company mid-2024

### Granola Usage & Feedback

- Discovered Granola through company’s #cooltools Slack channel \~1.5 months ago
- Primary use cases:
  - Weekly standups
  - Customer calls and summaries
  - Weekly customer catch-ups
  - Project kickoff meetings
  - Demo sessions
- Appreciates:
  - Automatic meeting detection for Slack huddles and Google Meet
  - High-quality transcription
  - Integration of manual notes with AI output
  - Background transcription during meetings
  - Helps with focus/attention challenges during meetings

### Feature Discussion & Feedback

- Folders/Projects Feature:
  - Prefers client/customer-specific folders over broad categories like “demos”
  - Concerned about privacy settings for different folder types
  - Suggested team collaboration features with Slack integration
  - Wants clear distinction between private and shared spaces
- Suggested Improvements:
  - Visual distinction between folders and tags
  - Ability to add custom folders beyond AI suggestions
  - Week-over-week pain point tracking for recurring meetings
  - Automated Slack notifications for new meeting additions

### Technical Interest

- Discussed AI model usage (confirmed using external models)
- Compared favorably to other tools:
  - Previous experience with MacWhisper
  - Similar quality to Cord
- Appreciates not having to manage local models

### Next Steps

- New features expected to roll out in approximately one month
- Team to continue developing folders/projects functionality
- Will address UI refinements for folder display
- Planning to improve shared workspace capabilities

2024-12-04T16:03:13.993Z
User Interviews
#### Andy’s quotes on what he likes about the mobile app

- Mobile app works “really nicely”
- “Best on-device piece of software” compared to 4 other tools he uses
- Particularly fast on Apple M4 MacBook Pro
- Team has done excellent job leveraging on-device capabilities
- Understands difficulty of hijacking audio on iPhone - notes this was wise to avoid

#### Login screen reactions

- Emphasized importance of separating:
  - Small team/Soho
  - SMB team
  - Mid-market/enterprise teams
- Different permission levels needed for each
- Enterprise likely using Okta/SSO services
- Small companies need fewer barriers

#### Homescreen reactions

- Need clearer separation between personal and team activities
- Recommended three distinct layers:
  - Private (just you)
  - Public (company-wide)

### Settings & Pricing Structure

  - Example: $20/month x 50 people = $2,500/month unauthorized spend

#### Pricing Recommendations

- Suggested pricing structure:
  - Individual: $10
  - Business: $15 (not $20 - “too big of a jump”)

- Consolidated billing matters less for smaller teams
- $10-15 expense charges typically don’t require approval
- Privacy/sharing controls should be available at all levels
- Recommended three-tier approach:
  - Granola Light (basic)
  - Granola Pro
  - Business (same features as Pro but with admin tools)

### Strategic Advice

- Need to serve two masters:
  - Customers
  - Investors who want rapid user growth
- Should be more explicit in communications about:
  - Privacy features
  - Personalization capabilities
- Positions Granola as “thought processing” not just transcription
- References successful experience with 6 exits including:

  - Grand Central (acquired by Google)

  - Dynamicsoft (acquired by Cisco)

15 Min Meeting between Shreman Shrestha and Peter Wilczynski
2025-03-27T15:04:38.693Z
Sales calls
### IT Security & Data Privacy Concerns

- “The more technology is important, the more knowledge workers get fucked by IT” - especially true when technology touches core IP
- Cannot use Granola professionally due to IT/security concerns around sensitive meeting content
- Current workaround: Shares plain text notes only, sometimes processes through ChatGPT
- Would consider using Granola if it could route through company’s own hosted AI model
- Valid IT concerns around satellite design IP and sensitive meeting content
- Needs stronger guarantees around data logging and handling

### Meeting Architecture & Organization

- Orchestra metaphor for meeting organization:
  - Current calendars are single-player focused
  - Need organization-wide view like orchestra score showing all instruments together
  - Meetings flow together like musical composition
- Meeting hierarchy and relationships:
  - Weekly meetings feed into monthly meetings
  - Monthly meetings feed back into weekly meetings
  - Example: 4 weekly meeting notes → summary for monthly meeting
- Current meeting types include:
  - Weekly prioritizations
  - Monthly roadmaps
  - Quarterly planning
  - Annual strategy/budget process

### Product Feedback & Feature Suggestions

- Key feature request: Create new Salesforce opportunities directly from meeting notes
  - Could command 20-40% price uplift
- Need to develop meeting ontology:
  - Use transcripts to automatically detect meeting types
  - Consider renaming “lists” to “types” or “flavors”
  - Help organizations automatically categorize meetings
- Current basic features:
  - Can check past recurring meeting notes
  - Lists/folders organization
  - Search functionality

### Distribution & Adoption Patterns

- Bottom-up adoption currently dominates:
  - Example: 70+ HubSpot users across different offices
  - No common pattern among users
  - Individual users adopt before enterprise discussions
- Note sharing behavior:
  - Users hesitant to share direct Granola links
  - Preference to copy/paste into Slack vs sharing Granola directly
  - Need to make sharing more “acceptable” in business culture
- No outbound or paid marketing currently drives growth

### Background

- Works at education research non-profit TNTP (600+ employees)
- Found Granola through Basecamp community recommendation

- Currently the only Granola user in their organization

  - Anonymous commenting feature

- Hesitant to share Granola links directly due to AI-generated content
- Would like:

  - Better integration between checklists and exported notes
  - Easier ways to track action items by person

### Transcript Usage

- Rarely references full transcripts
- Uses them mainly to:
  - Find missing context
  - Verify specific action items
  - Get more granular details when summaries are too general
- Appreciates having transcripts available but doesn’t need them on iOS

iOS App Feedback between Jonathan Mendoza and Robert Yang
2025-03-18T17:00:14.733Z
iOS user calls
### Background & Context

- Robert Yang is CEO/Product Manager of a startup called Mettle
- Uses Granola frequently during client and partner meetings
- Team includes coaches who have started using Granola for client sessions
- Gradually onboarding more team members to use the tool

### Current Usage & Feedback

- Primary use cases:
  - Capturing action items and next steps
  - Copy/pasting next steps into client follow-up emails
  - Querying past conversations for details
  - Sharing meeting links with partners who couldn’t attend
- Main confusion: iOS app functionality with phone calls
- Currently using desktop version for remote calls
- Desktop microphone picks up one-sided conversations when calls answered on phone

### Feature Requests & Use Cases

- Phone call recording is top priority request
- Key scenarios where phone recording is needed:
  - Car calls (driving in LA, up to 1 hour)
  - Walking the dog
  - Traditional phone calls rather than FaceTime/Zoom
- Interest in background noise handling for in-person meetings (coffee shops)
- Mentioned competitor “Oasis app” for voice recording/transcription

### Technical Questions & Next Steps

- Asked about template setup documentation
- Team will send follow-up email about template configuration
- Current iOS app limitations:
  - Only works for in-person meetings
  - No phone call recording capability yet
  - Can be used to review past meeting notes
- Phone call recording is on roadmap but timeline not confirmed

---

contexts.text:
iOS App Feedback between Jonathan Mendoza and Ziv Reichert
2025-03-19T11:00:25.146Z
iOS user calls
### Background & Usage

- Works for LocalGlobe VC fund in London for 5.5 years
- Previously worked in product/growth at startups and investing
- Has used Granola for over a year as an early user
- Currently uses Granola for 90% of meetings
- Team size at Granola is now 17 people

### Core Desktop Usage Patterns

- Uses chat feature as primary interaction method (90% of usage)
- Almost never reads the summary directly
- Takes notes during partner meetings on Mondays
- Uses hashtag feature extensively during meetings
- Dumps summaries into internal LocalGlobe CRM with Granola link
- Batch processes emails/follow-ups weekly (Friday-Sunday)
- Uses NotebookLM with Granola transcripts for deeper analysis
  - Example: Recent investment process - combined multiple meeting transcripts, deck, website into NotebookLM
  - Generated investment memo from combined sources

### Mobile App Experience & Feedback

- Uses mobile primarily for non-work contexts (e.g. doctor appointments, photography course)
- Key concerns with mobile app:
  - Lacks confidence indicators for transcription quality
  - Missing real-time transcript visibility
  - Too easy to accidentally start recordings
  - Cannot see all meeting attendees
  - Lacks desktop’s satisfying note generation animation
- Feature requests:
  - Add chat functionality
  - Implement voice interaction with notes
  - Improve search capabilities
  - Add ability to manually select specific notes for chat

### Future Considerations & Improvements

- Wants ability to chat with notes from multiple meetings
- Suggests weekly digest feature (“what are key actions from last 5 days?”)
- Data ownership concerns when using work email for personal recordings
- Requests ability to manually select notes for analysis
- Desires more dynamic interaction with mobile notes vs current static presentation
- Rarely edits summaries post-conversation
- Values speed and certainty in note generation process

---

Granola Beta iOS App Onboarding between Jonathan Mendoza and Erich Nachbar
2025-03-21T19:39:21.699Z
iOS user calls
### Current Usage & Background

- Has been using Granola Mac app for 3-4 months
- Runs all meetings through it with no complaints
- Only person on team using it currently
- Shares meeting notes via Discord threads (1-week TTL)
- Based in San Francisco

### Mobile App Use Cases & Motivation

- Primary use case: In-person meetings (2-3 per week)
  - Candidate interviews
  - Friend/networking meetings that become business connections
- Secondary use case: Meetings while in car/on the go
- Previous solutions tried:
  - AudioPen - unsuccessful, uninstalled
  - Plaud Pin - worked well but frequently forgot to bring physical device
  - Friends suggested switching to phone-based solution

### App Testing & Technical Details

- Successfully installed TestFlight version
- Initial account sync issue (resolved by logging into correct account)
- Key features demonstrated:
  - One-click recording
  - Screen-off transcription
  - Live activity timer
  - Push notifications for completed summaries
- Backend processing: Server-side transcription (not on-device)
  - Longer processing time than Mac app due to mobile optimization
  - Designed for handling unstable network conditions

### Feature Requests & Feedback

- Interest in search functionality:
  - Finding notes by person
  - Historical conversation tracking
- Suggestion for buffered transcription in future versions
- Will test multi-speaker handling and speaker isolation
- Expressed interest in widget placement (coming from Android background)

---

### Background & Current Usage

- Sophomore engineering student at Brown University
- President of Product at Brown (product management club)
- Takes 3-4 in-person board meetings per week for various clubs
- Currently uses notebook to take handwritten notes during meetings
- Found Granola through social media recommendation
- Uses for: club meetings, client meetings, mentor conversations, coffee chats

### Pain Points & Needs

- Struggles to focus on conversation while taking notes simultaneously
- Currently relies on handwriting notes during in-person meetings
- Wants transcripts to supplement light note-taking
- Recently discovered transcript feature and found it valuable for interview prep
- Feedback on transcription quality: wants accuracy level similar to WhisperFlow

- Clean, straightforward interface without unnecessary elements
- Lock screen widget feedback:
  - Liked the blue color scheme
  - Suggested adding pause button functionality
  - Recommended changing note icon to be more distinct from Apple Notes
- Transcript display feedback:
  - Prefers Mac app’s back-and-forth dialogue format vs mobile’s sequential format
  - Suggested “raw notes” label instead of “private notes”
  - Interest in speaker identification features for group meetings

### Next Steps & Product Questions

- Will test iOS app in upcoming in-person meetings
- Discussed premium version and meeting limits
- Agreed to provide additional feedback after testing
- Specific feature requests:
  - Better speaker identification in transcripts
  - Improved transcription accuracy
  - Pause functionality for recordings
  - More distinct app icon for lock screen widget

iOS App Onboarding between Jonathan Mendoza and Matt Raminick
2025-03-21T19:09:06.198Z
iOS user calls
### App Usage Feedback

- Matt primarily uses Google Meet for work calls over regular phone calls
- Phone calls typically brief (5-10 mins) and spontaneous
- Appreciates accessing recent call notes immediately after meetings
- Values the live activity feature, particularly for timing-sensitive situations

### Feature Requests

- Google Meet integration highly desired for mobile meetings
- Integration with Obsidian for note export (currently using iCloud sync)
- Interest in platform connectors for various note-taking tools
- Team documentation solution needed for SOPs, agreements, and meeting notes

### Current Limitations

- iOS app currently only supports in-person meetings
- iOS restrictions make call app integration challenging
- No real-time sync between mobile and desktop (temporary workaround: Command+R on Mac)
- Push notifications arrive 1-3 minutes after meeting ends on mobile

### Technical Details

- Live Activity requires double opt-in from users
- Notes sync eventually between mobile and desktop
- Notion integration currently available (though not relevant for Matt’s setup)

### Next Steps

- Matt to test app during in-person meetings
- Will receive email about upcoming sharing feature
- Agreed to provide ongoing feedback via email
- Matt to explore widget functionality for note creation

Granola Team Security
### Company Background and Requirements

- Granola is a 9-month-old AI meeting notetaker (Mac app) that transcribes meetings and provides summaries
- Currently 18 employees, aiming to grow to 30-40 people this year
- Need SOC 2 certification due to signing larger US companies
- First penetration test for the company
- Simple product architecture:
  - Mac app (primary)
  - iOS app (upcoming release)
  - NextJS website (read-only for viewing notes)
  - AWS Lambda infrastructure for API endpoints

### Security Concerns & Priorities

- Primary concern is data breach prevention due to sensitive meeting content
- Reputational damage from a high-profile user data leak could be “game over”
- Key third-party risk: Transcription service handling sensitive audio data
- Need to balance security with rapid iteration in fast-moving AI space
- Want to establish responsible disclosure program and bug bounty

### Proposed Testing Approach

- Cobalt offers continuous cyber attack testing vs point-in-time
- Internal team all security checked and police vetted
- Can perform both external and internal GUI testing
- Starter package: 60 days per year of testing
- Pricing: £1725 per day
- Example: 10-day engagement would cost approximately £17,250

### Timeline and Next Steps

- Aiming to start SOC 2 observation period by end of March
- Cobalt has March availability (90% certain)
- Actions agreed:
  - Schedule technical scoping call this week
  - Discuss bug bounty program implementation
  - Review detailed pricing and scope
  - Consider potential for ongoing security partnership beyond initial pentest

Granola Team
### Template Project Status & Design Decisions

- Decided templates should be user profile-based (different for VCs vs other users)
- Each template requires:
  - Name and icon
  - Description
  - Chat suggestions for folders
- Current templates are hardcoded and random
- Most user types will see similar templates, with VCs requiring distinct ones
- Templates should be company-relevant, not just individual-focused
- Action items:
  - Create draft template designs by Thursday
  - Test with real users to avoid misinterpretation
  - Consider renaming templates to “Presets”

### Positioning & Marketing Strategy

- Core feature focus is on folders and sharing infrastructure
- Hero image will showcase shared folders with smart chat analysis
- Hardcoded prompts will be prominent in marketing:
  - Blog posts
  - Marketing assets
  - Example: “What deals are we going to lose this week and why?”
- Despite being small features, these elements will be highly visible
- Need thoughtful implementation due to marketing prominence

### Technical Infrastructure Requirements

- Key infrastructure components:
  - Fast updates without database polling
  - Document synchronization
  - Panel loading optimization
  - Web authentication improvements
- Infrastructure priorities:
  - Permission request optimization
  - Lock screen redesign
  - Permanent opt-in after initial authorization

### Sharing Functionality

- Default sharing behaviour for workspace users:
  - Links accessible to organization members
  - Private folders remain undiscoverable unless explicitly shared
- Settings visibility:
  - Moving settings to sidebar
  - Sidebar to remain open in menus, closed in notes
- Key consideration: 85% of users aren’t in workspaces
  - Feature design should prioritize individual users
  - Need to maintain utility as a solo tool

### Launch Timeline & Next Steps

- Launch target: Next Wednesday
- Key blockers:
  - Synchronization implementation
  - Database infrastructure
  - Share flow design resolution
- Action items:
  - Vicky to schedule user calls
  - Review vision document
  - QA plan development
  - Verify default settings and behaviors
  - Linear task review and assignment

Dyanamic : Granola // Weekly GTM Session 2

Sales theory
### Sales Process and Negotiation Strategy

- When prospects mention a price range, they aim to anchor the highest option while getting the lowest rate

- Present 3 pricing options to:

  - Discover what’s possible in terms of deal scope
  - Set the negotiating space (zone of potential agreement)
  - Understand which variables they care about most (total contract value, per-seat rate, payment terms)
  - Enter negotiation being comfortable with the lowest option

- Example process:

  - Confirm scope: Are you turning this on for everyone (150 users) or rolling out over time?
  - Happy to walk you through formal pricing options

- Aim to close deals quickly, like the Ramp deal example

### Call Structure

#### Call 1: Discovery

- Ask for person with signing authority to join the next call
- “If I get you an option you like, what are the next steps you need to take?”

#### Call 2: Review Pricing (5 minutes)

- Show pricing to person with signing authority
- “Please walk me through the next steps”
- “We’ll show the order form once everything is agreed”

#### Call 3: Review Order Form Together

- Ensure everything is agreed before sending the order form

### Follow-up Email Template

“Following up on my last email, I know I gave you 3 different options. I’d love to schedule 5 minutes to review which option best aligns with your needs. We don’t want economics to be the prohibitive factor for moving forward, so I’m happy to be flexible if the rates are the only open questions. If there’s anything else product-wise, legal, or security-related, I’m also happy to review that. I just want to be a good partner in the remainder of the process.”

- Follow-ups should focus on what the prospect cares about

### Model Training Considerations

- Look at what Gong does for their model training approach

### Jo Handover

- Jo could take on a role similar to Youmna’s at Ramp

- Create a Superhuman team

- Set up a sales channel in Slack

- Develop best practices documentation

- Review calls together

- Use public channels for transparency

- Suggestion: “After you watch this Loom recording, I’m happy to walk through the details”

### What Youmna is Doing with Simon

- Develop goals on what we want to achieve
- Identify top accounts that signed up last week
- Send LinkedIn connection requests to key people
- Manage a “fake” Simon account for outreach (emails, LinkedIn requests)

### Additional Notes

- Create shared inbox (e.g., [sales@granola.com](mailto:sales@granola.com)) for team visibility
- Consider bringing Joe to these strategy meetings
- Set clear goals for self-service revenue (e.g., $5 million target)
- Implement white-glove service for most important users in the new year

---

- Secondary Problem: Audio recording issues

- Network Configuration Investigation

  - Enabled experimental API gateway feature

  - Checked system permissions for screen and audio recording
  - Verified microphone settings and permissions
  - Adjusted input levels
  - Identified default microphone selection issue

### Resolution & Next Steps

- Successfully resolved notes generation issue
  - Experimental feature implementation fixed API connectivity
  - Notes generation now working as expected

  - Identified correct microphone input
  - Customer now equipped with troubleshooting steps for future issues

Dynamic : Granola // Weekly GTM
2025-02-10T14:01:40.853Z
Sales theory
### Automatic Sales Replies

- Discussed setting up automatic replies to help qualify and disqualify leads
- Osman from Dynamic Growth Partners may have a solution; Joe has already met with him
- Aim to find a lightweight way to implement this
- Could potentially cut 10% of time spent on initial responses

### Business vs Enterprise Differences

- Current slide explaining differences needs improvement
- Approach: First write the text for enterprise features, then design the slide
- Key enterprise feature: Admin controls to enforce actions for the organization
- Business tier allows individual opt-out, while enterprise can enforce organization-wide

### Enterprise Free Trial and Pricing

- Discussed being strict with 30-day free trial enforcement
- Exceptions can be made on a case-by-case basis, but should be manually switched on
- Automated trial expiration creates an objective forcing function
- Consider adding a paywall for enterprise at the end of the trial period
- Discussed having three CTAs on enterprise homepage: Buy, Free Trial, Talk to Us
- Recommendation: Default to 30-day free trial as primary CTA

### Enterprise Homepage

- Should include:
  - Product features and capabilities specific to enterprise
  - Security documentation
  - Customer logos (if allowed by terms of service)
  - Contact form

### Enterprise Product Strategy

- Focus on IT requirements:
  - SSO (Single Sign-On)
  - Member management and permissions
  - Workspace visibility settings
- Consider meeting with the work OS team for enterprise-grade capabilities
- Potential feature: Identifying speakers in conversation transcripts
- Extra considerations for Healthcare (HIPAA) and Financial Services (SEC compliance)

### Sales Strategies

- Mercury deal: Example of “Mr. Thumbs” persona
  - Procurement person may be overreaching their authority
  - Action: Investigate who else is using the product within the organization
  - Focus on product experience and adoption when following up
  - Goal: Push for critical mass or consolidate purchases into a corporate license
- High-potential follow-ups:
  - Prioritize deals furthest to the right on the deal board
  - For non-responsive leads, it’s okay if they’re still using the product
  - Be cautious about pressing for purchases if it might reduce usage

### US Sales Hub Considerations

- Debating between San Francisco and New York for US sales presence
- SF pros: Closer to customers, aligns with board meeting locations
- NY pros: Easier for founders, closer time zone to London
- Consider management decisions and founder involvement in relocation
- Avoid “half-assed” moves that spread resources too thin

### Feedback for Shreman

- Doing a great job considering lack of prior sales experience
- Advice: Communicate less in writing, more verbally
- Keep using discussed tactics

2024-12-26T18:10:50.538Z
Sales calls
### Pricing Options

- Two pricing models discussed:
  - 12-month contract
  - 24-month contract
- If they push back on pricing:
  - Ask for case study opportunity

### Customer Requirements

- Team size: Over 150 people in the organization, expected to grow
- Security considerations:
  - Use Kanji for device management
  - Employees given company-owned computers
  - Cannot download unauthorized applications due to security risks
  - Manage significant amount of PII (Personally Identifiable Information)

### Use Case: Funding Sales Process

- Useful to have Granola inside funding sales process
- Typical process:
  - Merchant applies for capital
  - Multiple calls made with merchant (can have 10-12 calls per deal)
  - Need to analyze if merchant’s questions were answered satisfactorily
- Want ability to ask questions directly from transcripts within each deal

### API and Integration

- Current pain point: Lots of manual intervention required
- Desire for Granola to be automatically activated when microphone is engaged
- Want to integrate Granola data into Lendflow to attribute recordings to specific applicants
- API exposure timeline: Likely Q1 (probably spring)
- Potential integration steps:
  - Zapier integration
  - Public API exposure

### Compliance and Recording Consent

- 11 US states require explicit consent from all parties for recording
- Suggestion to look at Apple’s recording interface:
  - 5-second delay before recording starts
  - Automated voice announcement of recording
- UK laws less strict, but notification is recommended
- Granola deliberately doesn’t save audio/video, only transcripts

### Roadmap and Next Steps

- Request for high-level roadmap, especially for Q1
- Team to share roadmap in a couple of days
- Lendflow to review roadmap and determine next steps
- Possibility of connecting product teams to discuss integration

### Additional Information Requested

- PowerPoint presentation for pricing options
- Information on AWS regions used by Granola (for compliance purposes)
- Details on self-serve vs. enterprise lock-in options

### Potential for Longer-Term Engagement

- Open to discussions about longer-term partnership beyond initial 12-month contract

contexts.text:
Granola team plan between Granola and Dan Butvinik
2025-02-12T13:45:46.553Z
Sales calls
### /Current State & Context

- Growth Therapy currently has no formal note-taking solution
- Engineers discovered Granola organically and started using it
- Several employees already using Granola’s free tier (25 meetings/month limit)
- Users love the product and want to continue using it
- Current users have been asked to pause usage pending security review

### Security & Compliance Requirements

- Growth Therapy is a healthcare technology company requiring strict data controls
- Key requirements:
  - No patient data can be stored on external systems without BAA
  - All conversations must be treated as potentially sensitive
  - Data must either remain on company laptops or be covered by HIPAA compliance
- Potential solutions discussed:
  - Sign Business Associate Agreement (BAA)
  - Self-hosted or local storage solution
  - Granola currently working on SOC 2 compliance (expected next month)
  - HIPAA compliance planned after SOC 2

### Pricing Discussion

- Enterprise tier:
  - Starts at $35/user/month
  - 100 users: $31/user/month
  - 200+ users: $29/user/month
  - Includes IT admin controls
- Business tier:
  - $14/user/month
  - Annual plan: $12/user/month
  - Self-serve option

### Next Steps & Proposed Path Forward

- Dan to pitch security team on smaller targeted rollout:
  - Start with \~10 users (vs original 100-500 plan)
  - Implement strict usage guidelines
  - Run multi-month trial period
  - Conduct retrospective to evaluate broader rollout
- Shrey to:
  - Send pricing information
  - Check deletion capabilities with engineering team
  - Update Dan when HIPAA compliance progresses
- Team can self-serve signup for Business plan if moving forward with limited rollout

---

Fynd - shwetakanungo@gofynd.com and Ryan Francis
2025-05-29T09:30:10.001Z
Sales calls
### Background & Discovery

- Fynd’s cofounder discovered Granola through Twitter
- Currently using Granola for sales team external communications
- Fynd is the tech arm of Reliance Retail Group ($200B business)
- Seeking enterprise-wide deployment to improve meeting documentation and knowledge sharing

### Current Usage & Requirements

- Primarily using for external customer communications
- Planning 4-phase rollout:
  - External customer communications
  - All external communications
  - Partner collaborations
  - Organization-wide deployment
- Tech Stack:
  - Primarily Mac users (970+ out of 1000+ employees)
  - Google Workspace for Fynd
  - Microsoft Teams for Reliance integration
- Integration needs:
  - HubSpot connection (available)
  - ChatGPT integration (future consideration)
  - Potential integration with BOLTIC (Fynd’s workflow automation tool)

### Compliance & Security

- Fynd requirements:
  - SOC 2 compliance
  - GDPR compliance
  - ISO compliance
- Waiting for Granola’s SOC 2 certification (expected by August)
- Fynd runs own procurement process, separate from Reliance

### Deployment Strategy

- Initial POC:
  - Starting with 250 users (CSC and sales teams)
  - Expanding to additional 100-250 users by August
  - Unlimited users during trial period
- Biweekly check-ins during POC
- Need admin designation and deployment best practices documentation

### Commercial Discussion

- ROI-based pricing approach:
  - Year 1: Aggressive pricing to drive adoption
  - Year 2: Pricing based on demonstrated ROI
- Context: Reliance typically receives 80%+ discounts from major vendors (Microsoft, Google)
- Potential for expansion across Reliance Retail organization

### Next Steps

- Ryan to provide specific SOC 2 timeline
- Sign NDA
- Identify admin users
- Set up Slack connect channel
- Schedule follow-up before June 13
- Provide integration documentation for HubSpot
- Share Granola deployment best practices
- Future discussion on BOLTIC partnership potential

### Enterprise Plan Requirements

- 100 seats required
- SSO is a big requirement; Google Workspace integration not sufficient
- Privacy concerns: opt-out of model training, data retention policies
- Usage reporting and metrics needed

### SSO Implementation

#### How birthrights work

- Highly automated rollout of access
- ServiceNow ticket for granola access triggers auto-provisioning
- HR termination automatically removes all access
- Centrally manage access, applications, and provisioning/deprovisioning

#### SSO Pricing Considerations

- Agitated when companies monetize SSO as part of premium packages
- Encourage offering SSO in standard Teams package
- Reference: [https://sso.tax/](https://sso.tax/)
- Abnormal Security wants to be early partners in SSO implementation

### Granola Usage Vision

#### How they envision using granola

- Not for sales team (using CourseAI for go-to-market, integrated with Salesforce)
- Target: 400-500 non-sales employees
- Lots of demand for AI note-taking
- People directly asking for “AI notetaking”
- Potential use cases:
  - Post-meeting insights and action items
  - Integration with ServiceNow portfolio management for QBR projects
  - Status updates and action items for project manager reporting

#### How they’d separate people

- By department, function, project, initiatives
- Similar to current Slack channel organization
- Appreciate Slack integration, especially for private channels

### Next Steps

- Reach out when enterprise plan is ready (expected in a few weeks)
- Abnormal Security interested in being design partners for team features
- Prioritize content control over service operation data for enterprise plan

### Additional Notes

- Windows client development needed for broader enterprise adoption
- One-pager on enterprise plan requested
- Abnormal currently using Zoom for meetings, finding AI features lacking

Granola team plan between Granola and sreeja m 2025-01-24T13:59:05.070Z Sales calls

Sales Process Discussion

  • Considering changes to self-serve model vs. enterprise approach
  • Current pricing: $500/month mentioned for certain accounts
  • Challenge: Balancing automated sales with relationship building
  • Main goal is user growth, not maximizing revenue
  • Proposed threshold: 25-30 seats as potential enterprise cutoff

Security Documentation Updates

  • Reviewed security page content with Claude AI assistance
  • Uploaded Granola icon as placeholder
  • Identified gaps in compliance documentation
  • Not currently SOC 2 compliant due to being under size/revenue threshold
  • Team uploaded security documentation instead of just company icon
  • Need to address auto-deletion and retention period requirements

Enterprise Customer Requirements

  • Many customers have strict rules about data training
  • Need to develop clear policy around data handling
  • Enterprise differentiator: Custom data training agreements
  • Security questionnaires vary significantly between customers
  • Example: Scope didn’t require security documentation, while others need extensive verification

Strategic Next Steps

  • Hold off on immediate sales process changes
  • Plan to implement additional qualifying questions in sign-up flow
  • Need to develop automation flow for accounts under threshold
  • Will explore product changes needed for new sales approach
  • Consider separate workflow for 5-person teams vs larger organizations
  • Need to align with Mike about capacity logic

Key Decisions

  • Maintain current sales process until further evaluation
  • Add additional qualifying questions before making broader changes
  • Set tentative threshold of 25 seats for enterprise designation
  • Will require product updates to implement new qualification system

Sales calls
### Key Concerns from Plus Capital (RIA)

- Need indefinite retention of usage data (minimum 5 years for compliance)
- Currently limiting Granola use to low-stakes situations (e.g., initial intake calls)
- Concerned about transcript accuracy for high-profile meetings
- Require export capabilities for all visible data (compliance requirement)

### Current Export Functionality

- System exports both raw transcripts and enhanced notes
- Exports include:
  - Document title
  - User email
  - Meeting summary
  - Raw transcript
- No current ability to edit raw transcripts
- Summaries are editable

### Requested Product Changes

- Hide raw transcripts from users while maintaining summary visibility
- Continue providing summary exports
- No auto-deletion feature needed (conflicts with 5-year retention requirement)
- These changes would enable broader usage across more meeting types

### Next Steps

- Plus Capital finalizing internal policy this week
- Planning to set up enterprise plan by early next week
- Expected initial deployment: 9-10 authorized users
- Can purchase enterprise plan directly through Mac app
- No training required for enterprise plan implementation

### Follow-up Items

- Shrestha to investigate engineering effort required for transcript hiding feature
- Plus Capital to reach out regarding enterprise plan setup
- Open channel maintained for future feature requests and product feedback

Sales calls
### xSecurity Requirements & Concerns

- Emergence Capital and Langtech (security consultants) seeking to approve Granola for enterprise use
- Main concerns centered on data privacy and third-party access
- Recent updates to privacy policy:
  - No third parties can process or train on customer data
  - Enterprise tier allows complete opt-out of any model training
  - All servers are AWS-based in US locations

### Enterprise Account Details

- Enterprise plan pricing: $35 per user/month
- No minimum seat requirement
- Sign-up currently only available through Mac app
- Domain-based workspace management will automatically incorporate existing individual MCAP users
- Current integrations:
  - Deepgram for audio transcription
  - Anthropic
  - ChatGPT

### Security Infrastructure & Compliance

- SOC 2 certification timeline:
  - Submission for audit: March 2025
  - Expected completion: July 2025
- First penetration test scheduled for March/April 2025
- Internal security measures:
  - Audit logging for database access
  - Employee data access requires customer permission
  - Access limited to performance issues and legal requirements
  - Employee training and policies in place

### Meeting Recording & Privacy Features

- Key privacy protections:
  - No auto-joining meetings
  - Manual opt-in required for recording
  - Transcripts only available to meeting host
  - Explicit sharing required - no automatic distribution
- Recording stops when host leaves meeting
- Future roadmap includes:
  - Single Sign-On (SSO) implementation
  - Windows compatibility
  - Outlook integration

Dyanamic : Granola // Weekly GTM Session 2

Sales theory
### Go through emails: Follow up well + give/get

- Always think about how to elbow yourself through the queue
- Two key questions to ask:
  - Who are we working with? (executive/IC, IT vs compliance)
  - What does the company do? (is it a fit?)
- For deals of this size, we don’t do contract redlining
- Important to establish:
  - Who’s signing?
  - Forecast deadline?
  - Size of price?

### Attio

- Organized deals into stages: Leads, Replied, Screening, Follow-up, Customer Evaluation, Security Review, Contract Negotiation, Enterprise Free Trial, Push to Enterprise Self-Service, and Blocked
- Suggestion to add “enterprise” to deal names for clarity (e.g., “MetaLab - enterprise”)
- Focus on right-to-left prioritization to close highest priority deals first

### Enterprise in-product

- For enterprise free trials:
  - Review who’s using it and how many people should be using it
  - Identify who else is planning to use it or could benefit from it
  - Address any product or technical questions
  - Compare Granola to their current note-taking process
  - Determine steps needed for a purchase decision

### MSA and Contract Negotiations

- Clarity: Sent MSA and DPA for 10-15 seats with future expansion
- Follow-up: “Excited to partner. Once you’ve reviewed the MSA/DPA, can you help me understand what happens afterwards?”
- Always aim to understand the full process and next steps
- For pricing proposals:
  - Review live on a call
  - Offer three options (e.g., 20, 40, 60 seats)
  - More upfront commitment = lower per-seat rate
- Provide clear pricing tables in DOCX format for easy review

### Specific Company Discussions

Zego:

- Next step unclear; poor email communication
- Monthly commitment is set; send Stripe link and move on

Kliner Perkins:

- Likely doing due diligence
- CIO Mustafa involved; one person using the product heavily

Vercel:

- Propose: “If I were to give you the Field Eng deal, what would we have to do to get this signed by end of the week?”
- Verify MSA and DPA approval status
- Identify who can sign

- For small deals ($4,800), aim for same-day sign-up via Stripe link or credit card

- Follow up based on agreed timelines: “It sounded like the MSA review would be done today. Let me know if you have any questions or if I can connect you with our legal team.”

# Their background

- Lendflow - lending infrastructure provider (not brokerage)
- Raised $25M Series A
- 130-150 employees, all Mac users
- Process \~15,000 merchants/month
- Matthew is Inbound Sales National Account Director
- YC incubator alumni
- Moving toward Series B

# Pain points and needs

- Manual process copying text into calendar/Confluence
- Need better automation around meeting notes
- Heavy phone usage with merchants seeking capital
- Want holistic view of data within Lendflow
- Current tools: RingCentral, Confluence, Jira, Slack
- Need searchable transcripts across team
- Want API integration capabilities
- Need enterprise environment considerations

# Why he’s considering Granola

- “Context - we have so many siloed conversations about our product which is massively complicated”
- Need searchable language model behind conversations
- Want engineers to self-serve information vs going through chain of command
- Need queryable record of decision-making
- Quote: “To have a solution where we have a language model behind a conversation that took place to ask questions is really really big for us”

- Asked about segregated environment capabilities
- Questioned API availability timeline
- Inquired about data storage approach
- Interested in Zapier integration despite additional costs
- Asked about roadmap priorities

# Budget and timeline

- Open to 2-year agreement
- Current pricing benchmark: $20/user/month business plan
- Scale needed: 130-150 seats initially
- Potential to expand to 15,000 merchant interactions monthly

# Next steps

- Send enterprise pricing proposal
- Discuss integration possibilities
- Follow up on roadmap alignment
- Explore GraphAPI solution ([https://hasura.io](https://hasura.io))
- Schedule technical discussion around integration requirements

# Their role and their company

- Patrick Stokes is the EVP & GM, Platform at Salesforce
- Patrick has a background in building computers and is a long-time PC gamer
- Salesforce has a significant presence in London and other major cities
- Patrick used to live near London in Woking, Surrey

# How did they discover Granola?

- Patrick found Granola through the marketing tagline for people in back-to-back meetings
- He also discovered the Slack community

# What kinds of meetings do they use Granola for?

- Patrick uses Granola for meetings where he needs structured notes and summaries
- He has been testing the product for a few days and is impressed with its note-taking capabilities
- Patrick appreciates the ability to combine transcription with his own notes and prompts

# What kinds of meetings do they not use Granola for?

- Patrick expressed concerns about using Granola for highly sensitive meetings due to security concerns
- He mentioned a specific instance where he recorded a sensitive 1-on-1 meeting without realizing it, which made him cautious

# Walking me through a set of notes, what’s helpful, what isn’t?

- Liked the markdown feature in the notes
- Appreciates the structured output generated from combining transcription and personal notes
- Found the ability to identify and summarize mic tests impressive
- Mentioned that the transcripts should be more secure to be fully comfortable recommending the tool

# How often, when, how do you return to your notes?

- Did not specify exact frequency, but implies regular use given his role and back-to-back meetings
- Finds the structured notes more actionable and easier to review compared to raw transcripts
- Uses tools like Slack and Obsidian for note-taking and would like integrations with these platforms

# Please identify from the whole transcript and conversation, what their ‘jobs to be done’ are as they relate to meetings?

- **Practical**: Needs a reliable tool for taking and organizing meeting notes that works with his existing workflow
- **Emotional**: Wants to feel secure about the privacy and data handling of the notes
- **Functional**: Requires integration with other tools like CRM, ATS, Slack, Obsidian, and productivity apps
- **Social**: Wants to recommend the tool to colleagues but needs reassurances about security
- **Personal**: Appreciates features that resonate with his personal preferences, such as markdown in notes

# Additional Notes

- Mentioned Snipt podcast app for transcriptions: [https://snipt.net](https://snipt.net)
- Uses [Reader.io](http://Reader.io) for YouTube transcripts: [https://reader.io](https://reader.io)
- Uses [Writer.ai](http://Writer.ai) for summarization: [https://writer.ai](https://writer.ai)
- Suggested that for Salesforce to use Granola, data should be localized within AWS with strict network security
- Highlighted that the current weakest security link is the third-party prompt proxy
- Emphasized the need for compliance with legal standards regarding recording notifications

Granola User Interviews between Chris Pedregal and Marcus Rider
2025-03-26T14:37:26.686Z
User Interviews
### Current Usage & Value

- Customer calls are the “bread and butter” use case for Granola
- Takes notes during customer meetings in two ways:
  - When bandwidth allows: Creates structured framework during call
  - When overwhelmed: Dots down key points, relies on post-meeting organization
- Uses customer discovery template for initial discovery calls
- Uses hashtags to create section headers when possible during note-taking

### Note Taking Process & Integration

- Updates Salesforce after every customer meeting
  - “If I’m not updating Salesforce after the meeting, that was a bad meeting”
  - Uses Granola to distill meeting information before entering into Salesforce
  - Doesn’t copy/paste Granola notes directly - writes thoughtful, condensed notes
- Process flow:
  - Customer meeting (raw information)
  - Granola (helps distill to relevant information)
  - Salesforce (further distilled to high-density, actionable points)

### Follow-up Workflow

- Sends follow-up email after every meeting
- Current email generation feature needs improvement
- Follow-up email structure:
  - Initial calls: Meatier content, includes slides/recordings
  - Subsequent calls: Similar structure but more focused
  - Standard elements: Thanks, key points recap, next steps
- Prefers maintaining personal writing style/tone
- Open to AI-generated emails if they can mirror personal style

### Feature Feedback & Needs

- Heavy Salesforce integration is critical
  - All critical notes must exist in Salesforce
  - Would use Granola more if it auto-synced to Salesforce
  - Needs mirroring capability with minimal extra effort
- High meeting volume (11 customer meetings yesterday)
- Doesn’t want to organize meeting notes beyond flat list
- Hasn’t shared Granola notes with others
- Uses Salesforce notes to prep for calls and track what information is still needed

### Pricing and Concurrency Discussion

- Cost impacts on standard pricing: 100 concurrent streams = $5,000/year
- Total cost based on concurrency buffer: $1.75M
- Proposal to cut concurrency buffer in half
- Guaranteed capacity: 17,261 concurrent streams
- Up to 2x capacity (34,522 streams) available as “best effort”
- Logic in place for scaling; spillover logic for AWS if needed
- Buffer for concurrency is negotiable

### Technical Details

- Nova 3 is 0.5-1% better overall, significant improvement for keywords
- Currently have temporary concurrency allowance of 10,000 streams
- Options to reduce costs:
  - Prorate based on 3 months instead of 6
  - Consider self-hosted or Deepgram-managed solutions

### Pricing Structure

- Streaming rate same as current; volume increase significant
- Model opt-out pricing important; need to provide usage split
- Current proposal: Add to existing contract term
- Custom Granola option: $0.23/hour streaming rate, no separate concurrency charge
- Standard option: $0.13/hour + $2,500 per 100 concurrent streams

### Next Steps

- Sam to discuss with team
- Deepgram to provide Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis
- Follow-up meeting scheduled for Monday at the same time
- Deepgram to send recap and work on TCO based on 50 million hours projection

Call on Serverless + API Gateway | AWS-Granola
2024-12-05T14:40:20.068Z
AWS Engineering
### Current Architecture & Challenges

- \~80 AWS Lambdas currently in use, forming a “LambdaLith” architecture
- Client directly calls Lambda URLs, creating potential issues:
  - URLs could change if Lambda is accidentally deleted
  - Requires client upgrade to get new URLs
  - Creates disaster recovery challenges
- Want single entry point (e.g. [https://api.granola.ai/get-people](https://api.granola.ai/get-people))
- Successfully implemented API Gateway for regular HTTP Lambdas
- Key blocker: One Lambda requires HTTP streaming (for LLM responses)
  - Currently streaming from Vellum to client via [https://awslambda.stream](https://awslambda.stream)
  - API Gateway documentation suggests no native streaming support

### Proposed Solutions

- Config-based approach:
  - Create config endpoint or S3 bucket
  - Store Lambda URLs in config
  - Client pulls config when needed
  - Allows URL updates without client upgrades
- CloudFront approach:
  - Use CloudFront distribution with Lambda URL origins
  - Single entry point managed automatically
  - Simpler but lacks API Gateway features:
    - No versioning capability
    - No path management
    - Cannot decouple for throttling/scaling

### Technical Solution Details

- API Gateway streaming IS possible:
  - Requires proxy integration setup
  - Must configure response headers for chunked transfer
  - Works but “not beautiful”
  - Limited to:
    - 30-minute connection timeout
    - 10MB payload maximum
- AWS team will provide:
  - Code examples
  - Configuration details
  - Reddit post references
  - Related workshop materials

### Future Considerations

- WebSocket implementation needed eventually
  - Options: API Gateway WebSockets or AppSync
  - AppSync challenging due to DynamoDB requirement (currently using PostgreSQL RDS)
- Potential improvements:
  - S3 buffer for longer meetings
  - Multi-language support (currently English-only)
  - Compliance requirements to be discussed
  - Transcription/diarization improvements needed
  - Exploring Bedrock integration options

---

contexts.title: Chat with Svetozar Miucin (Solutions Architect, AWS)
contexts.text:
Chat with Svetozar Miucin (Solutions Architect, AWS)
2025-02-20T15:01:01.428Z
AWS Engineering
### Meeting Context

- Meeting with Svetozar Miucin (Solutions Architect, AWS) and AWS colleague Sadiq Azar
- Focus: Discussing Lambda and API Gateway scaling limits for Granola’s serverless architecture
- Granola is building an AI-powered notepad app with real-time transcription and summary generation

### Current Architecture & Usage

- \~30 Lambda functions behind API Gateway
- Current API Gateway usage: 731 TPS (average)
- Upgraded API Gateway quota from 10k to 50k TPS
- Core application flow:
  - Real-time transcription sync to backend
  - Note syncing
  - End-of-meeting summary generation via LLM
  - Third-party integrations (Notion, payments, emails)

### Lambda Scaling Mechanics

- Account-wide concurrency limit (shared across all functions)
- Burst limit: 1,000 new execution environments per 10 seconds
- Can reach 6,000 concurrent executions within one minute
- Concurrency ≠ requests per second (depends on function duration)
  - Example: 2 RPS with 1-second functions = 2 concurrency
  - Example: 2 RPS with 0.5-second functions = 1 concurrency

### API Gateway Burst Behavior

- Can handle full quota (50k TPS) instantly
- Additional 5k burst capacity as “leaky bucket”
- Burst capacity refills over time
- More favorable than Lambda’s burst behavior as no spin-up time needed
- Burst quota scales with overall RPS quota

### Optimization Strategies

- Provisioned Concurrency:
  - Pre-warm execution environments
  - Can use AWS Auto Scaling for scheduling
  - Costs \~25% of on-demand pricing
  - Takes 1,000 environments/10 seconds to scale up
- Account Segregation:
  - Separate accounts for free vs premium tiers
  - Individual quotas and limits per account
  - Strong isolation boundaries
- Asynchronous Processing:
  - Use SQS/Kinesis for non-critical operations
  - Helps flatten burst curves
  - Good for eventual consistency cases (e.g., note updates)

### Next Steps

- AWS to provide documentation for:
  - Setting up CloudWatch alarms for Lambda burst limits
  - Configuring Auto Scaling for provisioned concurrency
- Consider implementing async processing for suitable operations
- Evaluate account segregation strategy for different customer tiers
- Monitor API Gateway usage as it scales

# Email follow-up from Svetozar

**CloudWatch metrics alarms.** I've had some more thoughts on the alarms after our call yesterday, and I'd like to challenge our conclusion.

My take: getting an alarm on burst limit getting breached before it gets breached does not bring much value. This is primarily because the period of increase in concurrency is 10s. If you get an alarm within a 10s window, meaning "you're going to breach burst limits in 8 seconds" - what are your options? Moreover, when I checked Alarms, it looks like even though high-res metrics support 1s increments, if you want to use them in Metric Math in CloudWatch, it degrades the resolution to 10s (Today I Learned!).

Rather, I would propose you set alarms for concurrency utilization breaching a certain threshold (70-80% should be fine). IMO, this is more important, because it tells you - "Hey, your business is soon going to scale over your account/region quota, you should probably file for an increase."

In any case, apart from the obvious documentation on how to create Alarms (which you already have in your account), I would draw your attention to Composite Alarms - [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Create_Composite_Alarm.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Create_Composite_Alarm.html) These do pretty much what it says on the can - they let you compose CloudWatch Alarms to cover more complex conditions.

**As for the burst limit, I would advise using some of the proposed techniques:**

- Flattening the peaks using asynchrony. Something like what is described in this blog: [https://medium.com/@rplearn06/event-driven-architecture-with-amazon-api-gateway-amazon-eventbridge-and-aws-lambda-7b51d9f41841](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Create_Composite_Alarm.html) Here, note that EventBridge might drop your messages if the target is unavailable. I think for your use case, SQS would be better, with setting up a Dead Letter Queue to handle messages that were unable to get processed.
- (under Target Tracking) Automated Provisioned Concurrency target tracking: [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html#managing-provisioned-concurency](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Create_Composite_Alarm.html) This is the method I told you about, where Application Auto Scaling will work to track a target utilization.
- Scheduling Provisioned Concurrency for peak usage: [https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/scheduling-aws-lambda-provisioned-concurrency-for-recurring-peak-usage/](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Create_Composite_Alarm.html) this is if you want to control when the scaling happens.
- **Note on the two Auto Scaling options:** First one requires less overhead and thinking on your side. However, if you get a very violent burst - e.g. going from 0 to 5000 concurrency within 10s, you will still hit the burst limit. With the second option, where you schedule when the concurrency gets provisioned, you can accommodate for this by understanding trends and scaling before the peaks hit.

 

Finally, my mental model:

- Anything that returns an "OK" response - candidate for asynchrony
- Look into splitting some work into a separate account (e.g. free tier has its own sandbox, large tenants have their own separate sandboxes). This will lower the bursts.
- Optimize! Concurrency = RPS \* execution_time.
- Use the fact that you have 130 functions by optimizing only critical ones (hint: Rust is a very fast runtime)

 

Please let either myself or Manuel know if there are any blockers to moving forward, and we'll be happy to follow-up.

---

Automat-it <> Granola.ai: Architecture Overview and Database Performance Deep Dive
2025-04-14T12:18:53.307Z
Granola Team AWS
### Current System Architecture

- Running Lambda functions for all APIs
- Use CloudFront and API Gateway
- PostgreSQL RDS database with proxy
- Client-side transcription using Deepgram via WebSocket
- Offline-first architecture with client-side caching
- Heavy write traffic, especially for Google calendar events stored in JSONB columns

### Database Performance Issues

- Regular outages occurring lasting \~5 minutes
- Latest incident on March 25th at 10:42 AM
- Symptoms:
  - Database connections spike to \~800
  - Lambda concurrent executions hit limits
  - Query timeouts rather than connection errors
  - Heavy write load on Google events table (200GB+ size)
  - ACU utilization remains flat during incidents
- Vacuum operations:
  - Using PG_REPACK reduced table size from 34GB to 3GB
  - Current vacuum scale factor: 0.05 (default is 20%)
  - Auto-vacuum potentially not completing during high load

### Connection Management

- Using RDS Proxy for connection pooling
- Lambda functions reuse connections within same instance
- Current setup:
  - No deliberate connection management strategy
  - No read/write split (read replica exists but unused)
  - No queue system to manage traffic spikes
  - Connection timeout set to 10 seconds

### Identified Problems

- Write-heavy operations causing table bloat
- Google Events table particularly problematic:
  - Large JSONB columns
  - Frequent updates
  - Heavy data file reads
- No ability to intervene during outages
- Current architecture cannot handle traffic spikes effectively

### Recommended Solutions

Short-term:

- Implement SQS queuing to smooth traffic spikes
- Move large JSONB objects to S3 or consider DynamoDB
- Configure reserved concurrency for Lambda functions

Long-term:

- Implement read/write splitting
- Optimize database schema
- Consider implementing batch processing
- Review vacuum settings per table

### Next Steps

- Automat-it will:
  - Provide example implementations for traffic smoothing
  - Create proof of concept for Google Events handling
  - Help investigate specific database optimizations
  - Share AWS credits for testing solutions

### Additional Services Discussed

- Enterprise support upgrade available (15-minute response time)
- Well-architected review option ($500 or free with reselling)
- Potential for on-call support during incidents
- Cost optimization services through FinOps team

Troubleshooting AWS errors and lambda issues 2025-05-22T09:42:35.429Z iOS Department Meetings

Incident Overview

  • System outage lasted 90 minutes before detection
  • Root cause: Assembly AI API key issue
  • Primary impact on iOS users
  • Took 45 minutes to triage + 15 minutes to fix once detected
  • ~200 meetings affected during the outage

Detection & Response Issues

  • Dashboard showed green despite outage
    • Current metrics only show successful hits
    • Gap in metrics made it difficult to detect failure state
  • Debugging challenges:
    • Beekeeper client not working properly
    • Error messages weren’t properly stringified
    • Limited familiarity with Lambda systems
    • No visible changes in GitHub history
  • Customer Impact:
    • iOS users more proactive in reporting issues
    • Users cited importance of affected meetings
    • All affected meetings recovered successfully

Action Items

  1. Improve Monitoring

    • Create new metric for “unexpected errors”
    • Add alert for zero valid meetings in 15-minute window
    • Set up iOS-specific error channel to reduce noise
    • Investigate status page API integration for user-facing alerts

  2. Infrastructure Improvements

    • Implement queue system for assembly job submissions
    • Add retry logic for failed submissions
    • Review error handling in assembly integration
    • Document AWS Lambda debugging process

  3. Process Changes

    • Cross-post iOS-specific alerts to project-iOS channel
    • Create runbook for critical infrastructure components
    • Schedule knowledge sharing sessions for Lambda systems
    • Log all AWS configuration changes in prod-changes channel
    • Implement morning log review rotation between team members

Tradecraft security consultant call
2025-02-28T14:29:04.679Z
Granola Team Security
### Background & Context

- Granola is an AI meeting notes company handling sensitive meeting information
- Currently preparing for SOC2 observation period starting in next couple weeks
- Need pen testing as part of SOC2 but also want broader security assessment
- Tech stack:
  - Electron app (Mac currently, Windows in development)
  - iOS app in beta
  - Backend: TypeScript, AWS Lambdas, Aurora RDS
  - API Gateway routing to Lambdas
  - Multiple domains: [granola.so](http://granola.so) (original) and [granola.ai](http://granola.ai)

### Initial Security Assessment Recommendation

- 2 days consultancy recommended as first step (\~£1,200/day = £2,400 total)
- Can start as soon as next week
- Involves working alongside dev team for knowledge transfer
- Day 1 focus:
  - Run ScoutSuite tool to audit AWS infrastructure
  - Review architecture
  - Code review
- Produces assessment of current security posture and recommendations

### Key Security Priorities

- Domain cleanup needed - remove/firewall unnecessary [granola.so](http://granola.so) subdomains
- First day/last day employee processes crucial:
  - First day: Focus on practical tools (e.g. password manager) not security lectures
  - Last day: Maintain comprehensive system access list
    - Use Slack channel for tracking new system signups
    - Review access during offboarding
- Third party service risk management important given multiple SaaS integrations

### Incident Response Framework

- Four step process:


- Discovery
  - Create open communication channels (e.g. Slack)
  - Ensure clear ownership of reported issues
- Isolation
  - Contain impact (e.g. firewall compromised services)
  - Prevent spread to other systems
- Fix the issue
- Retrospective
  - Schedule within 1 month
  - Document detailed timeline
  - Capture learnings for improvement

Granola Team
### Key Updates & Fixes

- Database update resolved user preferences not saving:

### Customer Pain Points

- Note ownership/transfer challenges:
  - Increased requests for email transfer/changes

  - Individual plan notes belong to users
  - Business/Enterprise plan notes belong to company
- Windows performance issues persist:

  - General slowdown complaints

### Language Support Rollout

- Current usage: \~2,000 users
- Initial feedback:
  - Generally positive response
  - Portuguese localization issues (PT-PT vs PT-BR)
  - Transcription accuracy concerns in some languages
  - Summaries performing well despite transcription issues

### Feature Requests & Feedback

- Folders feature feedback:

  - User concerns about note quality comparisons
- Continued requests for:
  - Multi-language support improvements
  - Windows folders enhancements
  - Detailed transcription notes
  - Chat history
  - Outlook/Office integration
  - Export/import capabilities
- Diarization priority:
  - Users prioritizing diarization over real-time transcription

### Metrics & Performance

contexts.text:
Andy Workspace feedback
2024-12-04T16:03:13.993Z
User Interviews
#### Andy’s quotes on what he likes about the mobile app

- Mobile app works “really nicely”
- “Best on-device piece of software” compared to 4 other tools he uses
- Particularly fast on Apple M4 MacBook Pro
- Team has done excellent job leveraging on-device capabilities
- Understands difficulty of hijacking audio on iPhone - notes this was wise to avoid

#### Login screen reactions

- Emphasized importance of separating:
  - Small team/Soho
  - SMB team
  - Mid-market/enterprise teams
- Different permission levels needed for each
- Enterprise likely using Okta/SSO services
- Small companies need fewer barriers

#### Homescreen reactions

- Need clearer separation between personal and team activities
- Recommended three distinct layers:
  - Private (just you)
  - Public (company-wide)
  - Professional (specific team access)
- Suggested DocSend-style features:
  - Time-limited access control
  - Ability to revoke permissions
  - Example: “3 days to review, then access revoked”

### Settings & Pricing Structure

#### Settings page

- Raised concerns about unauthorized team upgrades:
  - Individual employees shouldn’t have budget authority
  - Example: $20/month x 50 people = $2,500/month unauthorized spend
  - Shadow IT issues - departments signing up independently
  - Need clear approval processes

#### Pricing Recommendations

- Suggested pricing structure:
  - Individual: $10
  - Business: $15 (not $20 - “too big of a jump”)
  - Enterprise: Contact for pricing
- Consolidated billing matters less for smaller teams
- $10-15 expense charges typically don’t require approval
- Privacy/sharing controls should be available at all levels
- Recommended three-tier approach:
  - Granola Light (basic)
  - Granola Pro
  - Business (same features as Pro but with admin tools)

### Strategic Advice

- Need to serve two masters:
  - Customers
  - Investors who want rapid user growth
- Should be more explicit in communications about:
  - Privacy features
  - Personalization capabilities
- Positions Granola as “thought processing” not just transcription
- References successful experience with 6 exits including:
  - Gips (acquired by Google)
  - Grand Central (acquired by Google)
  - Media Code (acquired by Yahoo)
  - Dynamicsoft (acquired by Cisco)

iOS user calls
### Background

- Works at education research non-profit TNTP (600+ employees)
- Found Granola through Basecamp community recommendation
- Has been using Granola for 1-2 months before testing iOS app
- Currently the only Granola user in their organization
- Works remotely with different states and school districts

### Current Usage Patterns

- Uses Granola primarily for committee meetings with multiple participants
- Main focus: Capturing action items and next steps
- Places phone on table during meetings for clear audio pickup
- Workflow:
  - Takes notes in Granola
  - Exports to Bear app for personal notes
  - Uses Craft for shared notes/collaborative editing
- Values simplicity and stripped-down feature set

### Key Feedback on iOS App

- Appreciates Live Activities notification as reminder to stop recording
- Manual note handling needs improvement:
  - Notes sometimes get overwritten/hidden
  - Wants better integration of manual notes within summaries
- Feature requests:
  - Needs ability to copy full text on iOS
  - Would like visual distinction between in-person vs virtual meeting notes
  - Wants better markdown support (bold text not carrying over)
  - Requests better checklist functionality that exports properly
- Privacy considerations:
  - Prefers subtle recording UI to avoid appearing like audio recording
  - Comfortable with voice recognition feature for speaker identification

### Sharing & Collaboration Needs

- Currently uses Craft for shared notes due to:
  - Live editing capabilities
  - Anonymous commenting feature
  - Low barrier to entry for collaborators
- Hesitant to share Granola links directly due to AI-generated content
- Would like:
  - Anonymous commenting on Granola web notes
  - Better integration between checklists and exported notes
  - Easier ways to track action items by person

### Transcript Usage

- Rarely references full transcripts
- Uses them mainly to:
  - Find missing context
  - Verify specific action items
  - Get more granular details when summaries are too general
- Appreciates having transcripts available but doesn’t need them on iOS

Covertswarm sales call
2025-03-10T09:46:30.309Z
Granola Team Security
### Company Background and Requirements

- Granola is a 9-month-old AI meeting notetaker (Mac app) that transcribes meetings and provides summaries
- Currently 18 employees, aiming to grow to 30-40 people this year
- Need SOC 2 certification due to signing larger US companies
- First penetration test for the company
- Simple product architecture:
  - Mac app (primary)
  - iOS app (upcoming release)
  - NextJS website (read-only for viewing notes)
  - AWS Lambda infrastructure for API endpoints

### Security Concerns & Priorities

- Primary concern is data breach prevention due to sensitive meeting content
- Reputational damage from a high-profile user data leak could be “game over”
- Key third-party risk: Transcription service handling sensitive audio data
- Need to balance security with rapid iteration in fast-moving AI space
- Want to establish responsible disclosure program and bug bounty

### Proposed Testing Approach

- Cobalt offers continuous cyber attack testing vs point-in-time
- Internal team all security checked and police vetted
- Can perform both external and internal GUI testing
- Starter package: 60 days per year of testing
- Pricing: £1725 per day
- Example: 10-day engagement would cost approximately £17,250

### Timeline and Next Steps

- Aiming to start SOC 2 observation period by end of March
- Cobalt has March availability (90% certain)
- Actions agreed:
  - Schedule technical scoping call this week
  - Discuss bug bounty program implementation
  - Review detailed pricing and scope
  - Consider potential for ongoing security partnership beyond initial pentest

contexts.text:
Granola team plan between Granola and Dan Butvinik
2025-02-12T13:45:46.553Z
Sales calls
### /Current State & Context

- Growth Therapy currently has no formal note-taking solution
- Engineers discovered Granola organically and started using it
- Several employees already using Granola’s free tier (25 meetings/month limit)
- Users love the product and want to continue using it
- Current users have been asked to pause usage pending security review

### Security & Compliance Requirements

- Growth Therapy is a healthcare technology company requiring strict data controls
- Key requirements:
  - No patient data can be stored on external systems without BAA
  - All conversations must be treated as potentially sensitive
  - Data must either remain on company laptops or be covered by HIPAA compliance
- Potential solutions discussed:
  - Sign Business Associate Agreement (BAA)
  - Self-hosted or local storage solution
  - Granola currently working on SOC 2 compliance (expected next month)
  - HIPAA compliance planned after SOC 2

### Pricing Discussion

- Enterprise tier:
  - Starts at $35/user/month
  - 100 users: $31/user/month
  - 200+ users: $29/user/month
  - Includes IT admin controls
- Business tier:
  - $14/user/month
  - Annual plan: $12/user/month
  - Self-serve option

### Next Steps & Proposed Path Forward

- Dan to pitch security team on smaller targeted rollout:
  - Start with \~10 users (vs original 100-500 plan)
  - Implement strict usage guidelines
  - Run multi-month trial period
  - Conduct retrospective to evaluate broader rollout
- Shrey to:
  - Send pricing information
  - Check deletion capabilities with engineering team
  - Update Dan when HIPAA compliance progresses
- Team can self-serve signup for Business plan if moving forward with limited rollout

---

Sales theory
### Sales Process and Negotiation Strategy

- When prospects mention a price range, they aim to anchor the highest option while getting the lowest rate

- Present 3 pricing options to:

  - Discover what’s possible in terms of deal scope
  - Set the negotiating space (zone of potential agreement)
  - Understand which variables they care about most (total contract value, per-seat rate, payment terms)
  - Enter negotiation being comfortable with the lowest option

- Example process:

  - Confirm scope: Are you turning this on for everyone (150 users) or rolling out over time?
  - Happy to walk you through formal pricing options

- Aim to close deals quickly, like the Ramp deal example

### Call Structure

#### Call 1: Discovery

- Ask for person with signing authority to join the next call
- “If I get you an option you like, what are the next steps you need to take?”

#### Call 2: Review Pricing (5 minutes)

- Show pricing to person with signing authority
- “Please walk me through the next steps”
- “We’ll show the order form once everything is agreed”

#### Call 3: Review Order Form Together

- Ensure everything is agreed before sending the order form

### Follow-up Email Template

“Following up on my last email, I know I gave you 3 different options. I’d love to schedule 5 minutes to review which option best aligns with your needs. We don’t want economics to be the prohibitive factor for moving forward, so I’m happy to be flexible if the rates are the only open questions. If there’s anything else product-wise, legal, or security-related, I’m also happy to review that. I just want to be a good partner in the remainder of the process.”

- Follow-ups should focus on what the prospect cares about

### Model Training Considerations

- Look at what Gong does for their model training approach

### Jo Handover

- Jo could take on a role similar to Youmna’s at Ramp

- Create a Superhuman team

- Set up a sales channel in Slack

- Develop best practices documentation

- Review calls together

- Use public channels for transparency

- Suggestion: “After you watch this Loom recording, I’m happy to walk through the details”

### What Youmna is Doing with Simon

- Develop goals on what we want to achieve
- Identify top accounts that signed up last week
- Send LinkedIn connection requests to key people
- Manage a “fake” Simon account for outreach (emails, LinkedIn requests)

### Additional Notes

- Create shared inbox (e.g., [sales@granola.com](mailto:sales@granola.com)) for team visibility
- Consider bringing Joe to these strategy meetings
- Set clear goals for self-service revenue (e.g., $5 million target)
- Implement white-glove service for most important users in the new year

---

### Customer Background

- Terazha Pitts from Ramp
- Has been using Granola since October 2022
- Previously satisfied user but experiencing issues since Christmas
- Currently forced to revert to manual note-taking

### Current Issues

- Primary Problem: Notes generation not working
  - App records meetings and creates transcripts but won’t generate notes
  - Issue persists despite uninstalling and reinstalling
- Secondary Problem: Audio recording issues
  - System only picking up one side of conversations
  - Inconsistent microphone detection

### Troubleshooting Steps Taken

- Network Configuration Investigation
  - Identified Cloudflare Warp as potential blocker
  - Added DNS configuration (1.1.1.1)
  - Enabled experimental API gateway feature
- Audio Settings Review
  - Checked system permissions for screen and audio recording
  - Verified microphone settings and permissions
  - Adjusted input levels
  - Identified default microphone selection issue

### Resolution & Next Steps

- Successfully resolved notes generation issue
  - Experimental feature implementation fixed API connectivity
  - Notes generation now working as expected
- Audio recording partially resolved
  - Identified correct microphone input
  - Customer now equipped with troubleshooting steps for future issues
- Follow-up needed regarding Cloudflare Warp compatibility
