AWS
### Current System Overview

- Running \~50 Lambda functions with constant weekly additions
- Infrastructure managed via Terraform
- Mono-repo setup using GitHub Actions for deployments
- Current AWS spend: $31k last month with 32% MoM growth
- API Gateway traffic: 336,000 requests/5 minutes (67,000/minute)
- Database size: \~0.5TB
- Using ARM architecture for Lambda functions

### Deployment Pain Points

- Full deployment cycle takes 20-30 minutes
- Code changes affecting common components require all Lambdas to redeploy
- Pipeline bottlenecks:
  - GitHub checks and tests: 4 minutes
  - Terraform plan: 7 minutes
  - Hitting AWS rate limits during deployments
  - Merge queue duplicate checks
  - Total commit-to-production time: >30 minutes

### Common Code Dependencies

- Shared components requiring full redeployment:
  - Authentication code
  - Type definitions
  - Database schemas
  - API handler wrapper
  - Global config with Lambda URLs
- Current build process bundles each Lambda separately using esbuild
- No tree-shaking optimization

### Infrastructure & Monitoring

- Direct to production deployment (no staging)
- Individual developer AWS accounts for testing
- Monitoring relies on:
  - Lambda error rate alarms
  - Client error tracking
  - Customer feedback for issue detection
- Primary AWS costs:
  - Database (largest contributor)
  - API Gateway
- Business growing \~10% per week
- Expected growth: potential 100x scale-up anticipated

answers.query: Across the workspace feedback calls, what were the recurring concerns about privacy, ownership, and personal versus team spaces?
answers.answer:
Across the feedback calls, the recurring concern was that **a team workspace could blur what was private, what was shared, and who controlled it**.

- **“Can my teammates see this?” needed an obvious answer.** Sukh explicitly worried about teammate visibility and wanted privacy settings or visual indicators. Andy said a sensitive banker conversation appearing on a “team page” would raise alarms—even if it remained private technically. Company branding alone could imply sharing. [7e8377b5-9153-475e-bcc2-e8ef4afd0fee] [d87cc517-beb9-4d68-bce8-2bf07a6ccd37]

- **Personal and team spaces were insufficiently distinguished.** Sukh interpreted “Create my own workspace” as a private place for notes invisible to his company and assumed multiple workspaces were possible. James similarly expected his own workspace to be disconnected from Zinc, while finding that the personal calendar and understated shared sections made the team homepage feel insufficiently communal. The ambiguity worked both ways: users could worry private content was shared, or fail to recognize genuinely shared space. [7e8377b5-9153-475e-bcc2-e8ef4afd0fee] [1689ee89-b60f-4e81-969d-020a5cd8f457]

- **Sharing needed explicit audiences and control—not just a personal/team toggle.** Andy proposed three layers: private to the individual, company-wide, and accessible to a specific team. He also wanted revocable or time-limited access and argued that privacy/sharing controls should exist at every pricing level. [d87cc517-beb9-4d68-bce8-2bf07a6ccd37]

- **Ownership and authority needed to be legible.** The workspace-design discussion worried that a shared space without an obvious owner or visible presence could feel awkward or “dead.” Andy separately questioned who had authority to upgrade a team or commit company spending, calling for approval processes rather than allowing any employee to do so. [1557e3dd-50c6-4ab3-b6f6-01d5905bbac1] [d87cc517-beb9-4d68-bce8-2bf07a6ccd37]

- **Team adoption should not compromise the personal product.** Mike cautioned against forcing team features too early: preserve the simple single-player experience, create workspaces behind the scenes, and reveal coworker content only after explicit opt-in. Sukh likewise envisioned proving individual value before pursuing company-wide adoption. [25b75e45-8cf1-4a5a-bfc3-c808e980ce34] [7e8377b5-9153-475e-bcc2-e8ef4afd0fee]

**Related later policy discussions made the ownership tension explicit:** the relationship between notes and workspaces remained ambiguous, particularly for notes created before joining a workspace. The team decided admins should not directly access private notes, while requiring admin consent for transfers out of Business/Enterprise workspaces—distinguishing privacy from control over data movement. These were later internal policy decisions, not conclusions from the feedback calls themselves. [90e8bb05-43c1-44a1-8b69-960ef73ea13d]

contexts.title: Decide settings & terms on data ownership & transfer
contexts.text:
Decide settings & terms on data ownership & transfer
2025-05-09T14:00:09.531Z
Granola Team
### Current Data & Ownership Model

- Users can technically belong to multiple workspaces, though this isn’t currently exposed in the product UI
- Need to clarify relationship between notes and workspaces (currently ambiguous)
- Crucial distinction: Should use “workspace” terminology instead of “company” for clarity
- Current data model allows individual users to have notes before joining a workspace, raising ownership questions
- Current billing ties directly to workspace status (Business/Enterprise vs Free/Individual)

### Workspace Note Transfer Policy

- Decision: Will require admin consent for note transfers from Business/Enterprise workspaces
- Free/Individual users can freely transfer notes between accounts
- Technical implementation:
  - Currently handling transfers manually via backend scripts
  - No immediate plans to build self-serve transfer features
  - Consider future export/import functionality as alternative to transfers
  - Copying notes may be preferable to transfers (leaves original intact)

### Admin Access Restrictions

- Decision: Workspace admins should NOT have direct access to private notes
- Rationale:
  - Aligns with user privacy expectations
  - Matches competitors (Slack/Notion only allow limited access for legal/compliance)
  - Preserves trust and company reputation
- Will verify legal requirements around admin access for compliance/legal cases
- Need to update security page to clearly reflect this policy

### Folder Sharing Considerations

- Current risks identified:
  - Users can share folders outside workspace before leaving
  - Folder admins can continue adding external users
  - New content added to shared folders remains accessible
- Need to evaluate admin controls for folder creation/sharing
- Will review how folder ownership transfers when users leave

### Next Steps

- Update terms and security page to reflect new policies
- Clarify legal requirements around compliance access with lawyer
- Document support response guidelines for:
  - Note transfer requests
  - Admin access requests
  - Folder sharing issues
- Continue handling transfers manually until volume necessitates automation
- Review folder sharing permissions and admin controls

contexts.title: Andy Workspace feedback
contexts.text:
Andy Workspace feedback
2024-12-04T16:03:13.993Z
User Interviews
#### Andy’s quotes on what he likes about the mobile app

- Mobile app works “really nicely”
- “Best on-device piece of software” compared to 4 other tools he uses
- Particularly fast on Apple M4 MacBook Pro
- Team has done excellent job leveraging on-device capabilities
- Understands difficulty of hijacking audio on iPhone - notes this was wise to avoid

#### Login screen reactions

- Emphasized importance of separating:
  - Small team/Soho
  - SMB team
  - Mid-market/enterprise teams
- Different permission levels needed for each
- Enterprise likely using Okta/SSO services
- Small companies need fewer barriers

#### Homescreen reactions

- Need clearer separation between personal and team activities
- Recommended three distinct layers:
  - Private (just you)
  - Public (company-wide)
  - Professional (specific team access)
- Suggested DocSend-style features:
  - Time-limited access control
  - Ability to revoke permissions
  - Example: “3 days to review, then access revoked”

### Settings & Pricing Structure

#### Settings page

- Raised concerns about unauthorized team upgrades:
  - Individual employees shouldn’t have budget authority
  - Example: $20/month x 50 people = $2,500/month unauthorized spend
  - Shadow IT issues - departments signing up independently
  - Need clear approval processes

#### Pricing Recommendations

- Suggested pricing structure:
  - Individual: $10
  - Business: $15 (not $20 - “too big of a jump”)
  - Enterprise: Contact for pricing
- Consolidated billing matters less for smaller teams
- $10-15 expense charges typically don’t require approval
- Privacy/sharing controls should be available at all levels
- Recommended three-tier approach:
  - Granola Light (basic)
  - Granola Pro
  - Business (same features as Pro but with admin tools)

### Strategic Advice

- Need to serve two masters:
  - Customers
  - Investors who want rapid user growth
- Should be more explicit in communications about:
  - Privacy features
  - Personalization capabilities
- Positions Granola as “thought processing” not just transcription
- References successful experience with 6 exits including:
  - Gips (acquired by Google)
  - Grand Central (acquired by Google)
  - Media Code (acquired by Yahoo)
  - Dynamicsoft (acquired by Cisco)

---

contexts.text:
Paywall expected behaviours & email transfers
2025-05-27T15:21:51.493Z
CX/Sales
### Current Email Transfer Process & Issues

- No formal process exists for email/account transfers
- Support team currently handles transfers manually
- Key issues with current approach:
  - Manual migration of docs only (folders complicate this)
  - Mobile build will make manual process more complex
  - Loss of revenue on subscription transfers
  - Lenny subscribers require new codes (becoming less viable as subscription lengths increase)

### Proposed Solution for Individual Accounts

- Allow users to change email ownership through settings page
- Requirements:
  - Must verify ownership of both email addresses
  - Need to handle Google login authentication specifically
  - Should migrate all personal folders and notes
- Shared content rules:
  - Transfer shared folders from external workspaces
  - Transfer personal coaching/external collaboration folders
  - Maintain access to content shared by users outside work context

### Workspace Account Limitations

- No email transfers allowed for Business/Enterprise accounts
- Process:
  - Email transfer option disabled while in workspace
  - Only becomes available after admin removes user from workspace
  - Prevents transfer of work-related shared folders
- Outstanding questions:
  - Need to investigate what happens to folders when users are removed from workspace
  - Need to understand technical requirements for updating Google login mappings
  - Need to determine exact behavior for calendar access after transfer

*Next Steps*

- Test workspace removal behavior
- Investigate technical feasibility of Google login remapping
- Schedule follow-up discussion about paywall implications

---

answers.query: What themes kept coming up in iOS app feedback, and which requests looked most actionable?
answers.answer:
## Themes that kept coming up

- **Make mobile capture effortless and dependable.** Starting a note felt “heavy” to Frankie; others encountered unreliable summary generation when leaving the screen, foreground-only audio uploads, or delayed desktop sync. The recurring need was to start quickly, put the phone away, and trust the result. [413c394d-66f2-49f0-9e50-491bb4486f69] [d60975a6-5a5d-46a6-80d4-d5c79e438489] [956e2a5c-95b6-46ae-b830-05f2bd3d26c2] [450b1e24-c606-4a32-a630-ed07b94563a9]

- **Make notes usable—not just captured.** Ryan reported manual notes being hidden or overwritten and wanted full-text copying, better Markdown, and exportable checklists. Cory wanted to copy individual items. Internally, editing and distinguishing human-written from AI-generated text were also priorities. [5c6cf2b4-8b88-4917-b103-a1087a31a1a8] [1b383447-9615-4ec0-b265-8f30c31d8d51] [956e2a5c-95b6-46ae-b830-05f2bd3d26c2]

- **Turn meetings into follow-through.** Action items were central to Ryan’s and Cory’s workflows; Frankie asked for cross-meeting action-item search, overdue/repeated-item flags, and organization into folders or spaces. Requests for to-do integration and exports to Bear, Craft, and Obsidian suggest users wanted Granola to fit existing workflows rather than replace everything. [5c6cf2b4-8b88-4917-b103-a1087a31a1a8] [1b383447-9615-4ec0-b265-8f30c31d8d51] [413c394d-66f2-49f0-9e50-491bb4486f69] [450b1e24-c606-4a32-a630-ed07b94563a9]

- **Notifications and Live Activities were valuable, but needed explanation and control.** Ryan liked the reminder to stop recording, and Matt valued Live Activities. Frankie and Cory generally disabled notifications; Frankie said a clear explanation would have changed his decision. Lee preferred a subtler recording interface. This was not simply a request for *more* notifications. [5c6cf2b4-8b88-4917-b103-a1087a31a1a8] [450b1e24-c606-4a32-a630-ed07b94563a9] [413c394d-66f2-49f0-9e50-491bb4486f69] [1b383447-9615-4ec0-b265-8f30c31d8d51] [eeaa7f47-c867-40d8-b182-1798327ec43b]

## Requests that looked most actionable

Based on specificity, recurrence, and explicit team prioritization—not confirmed engineering estimates:

1. **Fix basic note manipulation:** full-text and individual-item copying, faithful Markdown/checklist export, and clear human/AI text styling. These were concrete, bounded problems. The styling change already had a near-term action item; editing was explicitly required before public launch, though described as a larger workstream. [5c6cf2b4-8b88-4917-b103-a1087a31a1a8] [1b383447-9615-4ec0-b265-8f30c31d8d51] [956e2a5c-95b6-46ae-b830-05f2bd3d26c2]

2. **Improve permission onboarding and quick access:** explain the benefit before requesting notifications/Live Activities, help users discover widgets, and provide clearer controls. Frankie directly validated the explanatory approach, and Cory already found the widget useful. [413c394d-66f2-49f0-9e50-491bb4486f69] [1b383447-9615-4ec0-b265-8f30c31d8d51]

3. **Prioritize background reliability:** background audio upload and reliable completion away from the screen addressed fundamental mobile usage. The February sync explicitly identified background upload as a significant UX issue. The private-notes sync bug was reported fixed, so it should not be treated as an outstanding request. [d60975a6-5a5d-46a6-80d4-d5c79e438489] [956e2a5c-95b6-46ae-b830-05f2bd3d26c2]

4. **Scope a small follow-through feature before a full task system:** easier action-item extraction/export or a focused to-do integration would address repeated needs; global tracking and overdue-item detection were broader asks. [1b383447-9615-4ec0-b265-8f30c31d8d51] [413c394d-66f2-49f0-9e50-491bb4486f69]

**Less clearly near-term:** phone-call and Google Meet capture had strong demand but explicit iOS platform constraints. Mobile chat and photo attachments also recurred, but the evidence does not establish their effort or delivery timing. [d60975a6-5a5d-46a6-80d4-d5c79e438489] [450b1e24-c606-4a32-a630-ed07b94563a9] [956e2a5c-95b6-46ae-b830-05f2bd3d26c2] [413c394d-66f2-49f0-9e50-491bb4486f69] [eeaa7f47-c867-40d8-b182-1798327ec43b]

Current iOS App Usage & Feedback

    • Chris used it at a meetup for presentation notes

    • Trust in the app has improved significantly (~95% confidence)

Critical Features for Launch

  1. Notifications

    • Currently no notifications system
    • Will implement “Live Activity” notifications
    • Silent notifications for first 5 minutes of meetings
    • Critical for driving app adoption and retention

  2. Background Upload

    • Need to implement background audio upload
    • Current limitation: requires keeping phone open
    • Not data loss risk but significant UX issue

  3. Note Editing

    • Essential feature for users without MacOS app
    • Larger work stream than other features
    • Required before public launch

Immediate Action Items

  • Today:

    • Fix private notes bug
    • Add feedback button (iOS-specific email channel)
    • Implement analytics

  • By Monday:

    • Build basic notifications
    • Release to expanded test group (~500 users)
    • Add gray/black text distinction

Launch Strategy & Future Considerations

  • Will decouple iOS launch from Series B announcement
  • Initial release will be free with potential usage limits
  • Post-launch priorities:
    • In-app purchases/payment system
    • App Store ratings prompt
    • Search improvements (people, companies, titles)
    • Voice recognition/diarization features
    • MacOS companion app improvements

### Background & Context

- Cory is a product manager/consultant working with multiple companies in the AI space
- Previously built [Fulcrumapp.com](http://Fulcrumapp.com) over 10 years
- Currently consulting for companies including a legal tech company building CompFox for workman’s comp attorneys
- Found Granola through recommendation from medical field contact
- Chose Granola after trying multiple transcription tools (including Gong) - preferred its simplicity

### Current Usage & Needs

- Primary use: Converting action items from calls into tasks
- Uses Mac app regularly, wanted iOS version for mobile calls
- Main need: Transcribing phone conversations with clients
- Comfortable with call recording being announced to other party
- Doesn’t need to reference recordings later - primarily wants transcripts and action items
- Currently using Apple’s built-in call recording but finds it scattered across notes

### App Feedback

- Positives:
  - Easy access to meeting library on home page
  - Search functionality works well
  - Widget is useful and easy to access
  - Transcription accuracy is impressive
- Areas for Improvement:
  - Cannot copy/paste individual items from notes on mobile
  - Calendar integration could better handle group/team invites
  - Speaker identification would be valuable
  - Transcripts appear too broken up in the interface
  - Would benefit from to-do app integration

### Feature Requests & Technical Discussion

- Would like speaker identification capability
  - Willing to do 30-second voice training
  - Interested in using for family dinner conversations
- Notifications:
  - Currently opts out of most app notifications
  - Only enables for productivity-critical features
- Integration requests:
  - Direct integration with to-do apps
  - Better calendar integration for attendee management
  - API access for other services to use Granola transcripts
- Technical limitations discussed around Swift UI views and markdown rendering affecting copy/paste functionality

iOS App Feedback between Jonathan Mendoza and Ryan Fowler
2024-12-05T16:29:49.755Z
iOS user calls
### Background

- Works at education research non-profit TNTP (600+ employees)
- Found Granola through Basecamp community recommendation
- Has been using Granola for 1-2 months before testing iOS app
- Currently the only Granola user in their organization
- Works remotely with different states and school districts

### Current Usage Patterns

- Uses Granola primarily for committee meetings with multiple participants
- Main focus: Capturing action items and next steps
- Places phone on table during meetings for clear audio pickup
- Workflow:
  - Takes notes in Granola
  - Exports to Bear app for personal notes
  - Uses Craft for shared notes/collaborative editing
- Values simplicity and stripped-down feature set

### Key Feedback on iOS App

- Appreciates Live Activities notification as reminder to stop recording
- Manual note handling needs improvement:
  - Notes sometimes get overwritten/hidden
  - Wants better integration of manual notes within summaries
- Feature requests:
  - Needs ability to copy full text on iOS
  - Would like visual distinction between in-person vs virtual meeting notes
  - Wants better markdown support (bold text not carrying over)
  - Requests better checklist functionality that exports properly
- Privacy considerations:
  - Prefers subtle recording UI to avoid appearing like audio recording
  - Comfortable with voice recognition feature for speaker identification

### Sharing & Collaboration Needs

- Currently uses Craft for shared notes due to:
  - Live editing capabilities
  - Anonymous commenting feature
  - Low barrier to entry for collaborators
- Hesitant to share Granola links directly due to AI-generated content
- Would like:
  - Anonymous commenting on Granola web notes
  - Better integration between checklists and exported notes
  - Easier ways to track action items by person

### Transcript Usage

- Rarely references full transcripts
- Uses them mainly to:
  - Find missing context
  - Verify specific action items
  - Get more granular details when summaries are too general
- Appreciates having transcripts available but doesn’t need them on iOS

---

answers.query: What issues should the next on-call engineer watch based on the March on-call handovers?
answers.answer:
Based on the **March 2–3 handovers**, the next on-call engineer should watch:

### Open issues and recurring alerts
- **Metadata-fetching Lambda errors:** A significant, unexpected error spike needs investigation. Rising Lambda concurrency and spiky duration were otherwise considered expected. [5cb18b82-03b6-4003-83f4-772286673426]
- **Aurora capacity / possible throttling:** AWS was being consulted, and capacity scaling might need adjustment. The notes disagree on the metric—March 3 reports **100% ACU utilization**, while March 2 mentions a **2% usage threshold**—so verify the dashboard rather than relying on either figure alone. [5cb18b82-03b6-4003-83f4-772286673426] [39aab9b3-ceb8-44d0-8247-72e56659d56c]
- **Secrets Manager monitoring gap:** The access alarm was temporarily disabled because Lambda environment-variable size limits had been reached. A better secrets-caching solution was still needed. [5cb18b82-03b6-4003-83f4-772286673426]
- **Queue validation failures:** A customer email containing `%` fails Zod validation in two queues and can trigger alarms. Deleting dead-letter messages was discussed, but the evidence does not establish a permanent fix. [5cb18b82-03b6-4003-83f4-772286673426] [76acc661-0ee1-4311-89de-7cb9b9621ce0]
- **Avatar API credits:** The alert triggers below **100,000 credits**. Check telemetry/graphs first, then escalate to **Jim**, who has the direct link to contact Sam for top-ups. No alert-tolerance change was considered necessary. [5cb18b82-03b6-4003-83f4-772286673426] [39aab9b3-ceb8-44d0-8247-72e56659d56c]

### Lower-priority / recurrence watch
- **Slack alarm noise:** Its threshold was adjusted and it should now be quieter. [5cb18b82-03b6-4003-83f4-772286673426]
- **Stripe subscription edge case:** Immediate cancellation after creation caused a subscription fetch to fail. The affected record was removed, resolving that incident, but the root cause was not established. Watch for recurrence rather than treating it as an active outage. [76acc661-0ee1-4311-89de-7cb9b9621ce0]
- **Motion flakiness:** Noted, but judged non-critical. [39aab9b3-ceb8-44d0-8247-72e56659d56c]

**Shift essentials:** Cover **9 AM–9 PM**, monitor pages and the ops channel, acknowledge pages within **30 minutes** before automatic escalation, escalate unfamiliar issues, and arrange coverage for planned unavailability. Use the incident-escalation function for after-hours issues. [5cb18b82-03b6-4003-83f4-772286673426] [39aab9b3-ceb8-44d0-8247-72e56659d56c]

answers.query: What did Granola agree to change for Ramp, and what pricing/compliance terms were discussed?
answers.answer:
At the **October 2, 2024 Ramp meeting**, Granola committed to two immediate changes and discussed Enterprise pricing and a compliance grace period.

### Changes for Ramp
- **Disable training on Ramp conversations**, including audio/transcripts, by Granola and its subprocessors/providers.
- **Disable external sharing links**, with both changes targeted for the next day. Internal sharing within Ramp was intended to remain available; the transcript describes Ramp-only link access as something Granola would build over time. [659b81c4-5e11-406f-a60e-6f38314ef74f]

### Pricing and compliance terms
- **Enterprise pricing of $25/user/month, up from $10/user/month**, reflecting additional security controls and provider-training opt-outs. Ramp still needed to confirm the price internally and determine the total number of users across teams. [659b81c4-5e11-406f-a60e-6f38314ef74f]
- Granola proposed signing the contract with a **60-day window to meet the remaining compliance requirements**. Insurance was the main outstanding item and could take longer to obtain. Paul Yoo was to consult Ramp’s legal team about the clause, so the evidence does not establish final legal approval or contract execution. [659b81c4-5e11-406f-a60e-6f38314ef74f]

### Pricing Options

- Two pricing models discussed:

### Customer Requirements

- Team size: Over 150 people in the organization, expected to grow
- Security considerations:
  - Use Kanji for device management
  - Employees given company-owned computers
  - Cannot download unauthorized applications due to security risks
  - Manage significant amount of PII (Personally Identifiable Information)

- Useful to have Granola inside funding sales process
- Typical process:
  - Merchant applies for capital
  - Multiple calls made with merchant (can have 10-12 calls per deal)

- Current pain point: Lots of manual intervention required
- Desire for Granola to be automatically activated when microphone is engaged
- Want to integrate Granola data into Lendflow to attribute recordings to specific applicants
- API exposure timeline: Likely Q1 (probably spring)
- Potential integration steps:
  - Zapier integration
  - Public API exposure

### Compliance and Recording Consent

- 11 US states require explicit consent from all parties for recording
- Suggestion to look at Apple’s recording interface:
  - 5-second delay before recording starts
  - Automated voice announcement of recording
- UK laws less strict, but notification is recommended
- Granola deliberately doesn’t save audio/video, only transcripts

### Roadmap and Next Steps

- Request for high-level roadmap, especially for Q1
- Team to share roadmap in a couple of days
- Lendflow to review roadmap and determine next steps
- Possibility of connecting product teams to discuss integration

- PowerPoint presentation for pricing options
- Information on AWS regions used by Granola (for compliance purposes)
- Details on self-serve vs. enterprise lock-in options

### Potential for Longer-Term Engagement

- Open to discussions about longer-term partnership beyond initial 12-month contract

answers.query: What procurement and security requirements did Kraken raise before broader Granola rollout?
answers.answer:
In the December 4, 2024 discussion, Kraken’s procurement lead Jeff raised these requirements and readiness questions:

- **Enforced SSO with Okta integration.** Granola did not yet support Okta; it was planned for the next couple of months. [19b2d83f-ee76-47cb-a2d8-34f744239ae4]
- **Security review before approval.** Even short-term individual-user approval was pending Kraken’s security-team review. SOC 2 readiness was discussed: Granola reported its technical checklist complete, policies still in development, and expected completion in January/February. The notes do not explicitly establish SOC 2 certification as a hard rollout condition. [19b2d83f-ee76-47cb-a2d8-34f744239ae4]
- **Enterprise contracting and billing readiness.** They discussed enterprise license agreements and individual versus team-wide payment options. Granola had completed one custom agreement and expected a standardized agreement in roughly a week; the notes do not record specific Kraken contractual clauses or billing mandates. [19b2d83f-ee76-47cb-a2d8-34f744239ae4]

The planned path was to revisit broader adoption in “a couple of months,” after Granola’s security and admin improvements, while individual use remained subject to security approval. [19b2d83f-ee76-47cb-a2d8-34f744239ae4]

Introduction Granola - Specialist for Security Review
2025-02-14T16:08:22.192Z
AWS Security Engineering
### Current Security Setup and Gaps

- Currently using basic dependency checks integrated with GitHub build tools for TypeScript
- Infrastructure includes \~100 Lambda functions with two main entry points:
  - Direct Lambda URLs (legacy)
  - API Gateway (new implementation)
- Multiple client applications: macOS (Electron), iOS app in development, web app, with Windows and Android planned
- No Web Application Firewall (WAF) currently implemented
- No Shield Advanced in place
- Multiple third-party service integrations (\~10+)

### Recommended Security Implementations

- AWS WAF Implementation:
  - Costs approximately $100/month per ACL
  - Includes managed rules covering OWASP Top 10
  - Critical for preventing 98% of common data breaches
  - Required for SOC 2 compliance
- AWS Audit Manager:
  - Run temporarily to avoid high costs
  - Provides SOC 2 baseline assessment
  - Generates findings report for prioritized actions
- Security Scanning Tools:
  - DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) recommended for frontend
  - Suggested tool: Burp Suite for regular vulnerability scanning
  - SAST (Static Application Security Testing) for code-base scanning

### Current Compliance Status

- Working with Vanta for SOC 2 compliance:
  - Approximately 50% complete on automatic testing and policies
  - Target completion: 2 weeks
- Engaged Work Street for:
  - VC requirements
  - Additional compliance support
  - Comprehensive penetration testing

### Next Steps and Action Items

- Enable AWS WAF immediately:
  - Calculate costs using AWS pricing calculator
  - Implement before penetration testing
- Run AWS Audit Manager:
  - Enable SOC 2 baseline assessment
  - Generate report
  - Disable after completion (within 24 hours)
- Implement regular security scanning:
  - Set up weekly/monthly DAST scanning process
  - Establish vulnerability remediation workflow
- Continue SOC 2 compliance work with Vanta and Work Street

answers.query: What compliance needs did Plus Capital have, and how did the follow-up change the product ask?
answers.answer:
Plus Capital’s ask shifted from **retaining and exporting transcripts** to **hiding raw transcripts while keeping editable summaries visible and exportable—without deleting retained data**.

### Initial compliance needs — March 7
As a US registered investment adviser with a privacy-sensitive client base, Plus Capital needed:
- **Five-year record retention**, with the ability to download all transcripts; quarterly downloads were discussed because the process was manual.
- **Enterprise-wide controls** over data and settings, including opting out of internal model training.
- **Automatic consent messaging**, preferably a visible chat message rather than a checkbox. The discussion also specified that only transcripts—not audio/video—were retained. [d74a5e93-08af-4ffe-84ec-915704104186]

### How the March 12 follow-up changed the product ask
The follow-up clarified that they wanted **indefinite retention, with five years as the compliance minimum**, and exports of **all data visible to users**. But they were concerned about transcript accuracy in high-profile meetings and were limiting Granola to low-stakes uses such as initial intake calls. Raw transcripts could not be edited, whereas summaries could. [07448f73-6890-4533-8931-65051a385e1c]

The resulting request was to **hide raw transcripts from users, preserve summary visibility, and continue summary exports**. They explicitly did **not** need auto-deletion because it conflicted with their retention requirement. This change would enable broader meeting usage; Shrestha’s next step was to investigate the engineering effort for transcript hiding, not a commitment that it was already available. ### Current Security Infrastructure

- Encryption protocols: AES-256 for data at rest, TLS 1.2+ for data in transit
- Internal infrastructure team manages encryption keys with strict access controls
- Role-based access control system for internal data access
- Regular security audits: quarterly internal, annual third-party
- Penetration testing conducted annually by NCC Group/Rapid7
- AWS provides primary cloud infrastructure

### Compliance & Certifications

- Current certifications: SOC 2, GDPR compliant
- ISO 27001 certification in progress
- No current HIPAA or FedRAMP certification
- All subprocessors (AWS, analytics providers) maintain GDPR and SOC 2 compliance
- Detailed activity logs available upon request

### Data Management Policies

- Region-specific data residency available through AWS
- Backup retention: 6 months to 3 years (client-specific)
- Data deletion protocols:
  - Standard: 30 days post-contract termination
  - Expedited: Within 72 hours upon request
  - Deletion certificate provided upon completion

### Incident Response & Security Protocols

- 24-hour breach notification policy
- Dedicated incident response team
- Transparent communication throughout incident management
- Subprocessor information publicly available on trust page
- Clear documentation of all security measures and compliance standards

### Next Steps

- AllFound to send comprehensive compliance documentation
- Schedule follow-up meeting to address remaining regulatory questions
- Internal discussion needed by Intellisolutions regarding regulatory requirements
- Compliance team to review FedRAMP certification request

Shre (Granola) / Trevor (Maverick)

Sales calls
### SEC Compliance & Books & Records Requirements

- SEC interprets books & records requirements very broadly
- Includes all electronic communications, trading information, research meeting minutes
- Must retain records for 7 years according to current policy
- Some meetings deliberately not minuted to avoid SEC scrutiny
- Meeting minute takers trained specifically for “regulator-friendly” documentation
- Global Relay integration: Currently captures emails, Bloomberg chats, Microsoft chats
- Received list of flagged keywords used for compliance monitoring

### Key Concerns with AI Note-Taking

- Main fears: tone interpretation, mistakes, and regulatory implications
- Raw transcripts likely require retention if saved to systems
- Even 100% accurate transcripts problematic due to loss of tone/context
- Reference case: Deerfield (02/2017) insider trading case highlighted problematic electronic communications
- Specific concern about back-to-back meetings leading to inadequate note review

### Potential Implementation Requirements

- RIA (SEC) compliance considerations
- Must be able to edit notes before they are “saved”
- Require “box to confirm” functionality
- Need clear policies around notification of tool usage
- Preference for forced/automatic notification rather than relying on employee compliance
- Would only initially implement for venture/portfolio company meetings (lower risk)

### Proposed Solution Parameters

- No transcript storage/display - summary notes only
- Need ability to edit summaries before system storage
- Require clear process for where/how data is saved
- Consider specialized enterprise subscription without transcript features
- Must notify all parties (similar to call recording requirements)
- Could start with limited rollout for low-risk meetings only

contexts.title: Granola User Interviews between Chris Pedregal and Marcus Rider
contexts.text:
Granola User Interviews between Chris Pedregal and Marcus Rider
2025-03-26T14:37:26.686Z
User Interviews
### Current Usage & Value

- Customer calls are the “bread and butter” use case for Granola
- Takes notes during customer meetings in two ways:
  - When bandwidth allows: Creates structured framework during call
  - When overwhelmed: Dots down key points, relies on post-meeting organization
- Uses customer discovery template for initial discovery calls
- Uses hashtags to create section headers when possible during note-taking

### Note Taking Process & Integration

- Updates Salesforce after every customer meeting
  - “If I’m not updating Salesforce after the meeting, that was a bad meeting”
  - Uses Granola to distill meeting information before entering into Salesforce
  - Doesn’t copy/paste Granola notes directly - writes thoughtful, condensed notes
- Process flow:
  - Customer meeting (raw information)
  - Granola (helps distill to relevant information)
  - Salesforce (further distilled to high-density, actionable points)

### Follow-up Workflow

- Sends follow-up email after every meeting
- Current email generation feature needs improvement
- Follow-up email structure:
  - Initial calls: Meatier content, includes slides/recordings
  - Subsequent calls: Similar structure but more focused
  - Standard elements: Thanks, key points recap, next steps
- Prefers maintaining personal writing style/tone
- Open to AI-generated emails if they can mirror personal style

### Feature Feedback & Needs

- Heavy Salesforce integration is critical
  - All critical notes must exist in Salesforce
  - Would use Granola more if it auto-synced to Salesforce
  - Needs mirroring capability with minimal extra effort
- High meeting volume (11 customer meetings yesterday)
- Doesn’t want to organize meeting notes beyond flat list
- Hasn’t shared Granola notes with others
- Uses Salesforce notes to prep for calls and track what information is still needed
